title: Peer Prediction for Learning Agents
headline: Confirmed finding: Sequential binary correlated agreement achieves almost-sure convergence of the realised pure-strategy sequences to truth-telling or flipping whenever both agents use fixed reward-based update functions satisfying Assumptions 3.3-3.5.

work.title: Peer Prediction for Learning Agents

claims.label: Theorem 4.1 truthful convergence
claims.page: Main paper; decisive proof transition in supplement p. 31
claims.gist: Sequential binary correlated agreement achieves almost-sure convergence of the realised pure-strategy sequences to truth-telling or flipping whenever both agents use fixed reward-based update functions satisfying Assumptions 3.3-3.5.
claims.statement: Sequential binary correlated agreement achieves almost-sure convergence of the realised pure-strategy sequences to truth-telling or flipping whenever both agents use fixed reward-based update functions satisfying Assumptions 3.3-3.5.
conditions: Signals are i.i.d. with full support and the paper's positive-correlation condition.
Each agent uses one fixed reward-based update function satisfying exchangeability, order preservation and full exploitation.
claims.quantifiers: For every admissible signal distribution and every pair of update functions satisfying Assumptions 3.3-3.5.

result.summary: An admissible fixed update rule keeps each uninformative pure strategy at a nonsummable probability, so realised pure play fails to converge almost surely; the theorem's probability-one conclusion becomes probability zero.
result.witness: An admissible fixed update rule keeps each uninformative pure strategy at a nonsummable probability, so realised pure play fails to converge almost surely; the theorem's probability-one conclusion becomes probability zero.
result.argument: Assumption-by-assumption hostile validation of the proposed inverse-gap update rule, reward bounds, conditional Borel-Cantelli argument, theorem quantifiers and supplement proof transition. Limits: Does not refute earlier reward-process lemmas, named algorithms generally, mixed-strategy probability convergence, or Theorems 3.1/3.2.
not_claimed: The counterexample targets the theorem's unrestricted algorithm class and realised-action convergence, not all familiar learning algorithms or weaker convergence notions.
